claim: Human pluripotent-stem-cell-derived oligodendrocyte spheroids were reported to recapitulate stages of oligodendrocyte maturation and permit live observation of migration, myelination-related development, and injury response, establishing an external technical precedent for a human myelin-support assay.
future_grounding_route: Use as platform-feasibility context only. Project use requires independent donor replication, prespecified functional outcomes, blinded imaging, and a direct comparison with simpler co-culture before accepting organoid complexity.
project_use: External precedent for a human oligodendrocyte/myelin readout downstream of microglial perturbation; not evidence for an MS mechanism.
relationship_note: The platform provides a functional tissue-side readout but is developmental and cannot by itself model chronic adult MS progression.

source.citation: Marton et al. Differentiation and maturation of oligodendrocytes in human three-dimensional neural cultures. Nature Neuroscience. 2019.
source.label: Human oligodendrocyte spheroids

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: Publisher page metadata and short paraphrase only
source_terms.reuse_notes: Store bibliographic metadata and a short paraphrase; do not redistribute article text.

why_unverifiable: The project has not reproduced the spheroid platform or rerun its source experiments.
